# Feature: Game shell and deterministic core

<!-- Generated by the project-manager tool from pm.yml. Do not edit by hand; the store is the source of truth. -->

## Goal

Provide the game page that every later mechanic plugs into. The engine step function is pure and deterministic: given the initial level plus the ordered, timestamped input log, the same run always produces the same states. The timer is a real counting clock reproduced in replay from recorded t_ms timestamps, never from unrecorded wall-clock reads.

## User Story

**As a** player
**I want** to open the game, pick a level, and play
**So that** later mechanics have a deterministic, recordable home.

## High-Level Use Case

Player opens the game URL, chooses a level or Test Level from the game menu, and plays with the keyboard. Every play is recorded as a JSONL session from the first playable build.

## Player-Facing Behavior

- Given a level file, when the game loads, then it renders that level.
- Given the same initial level and the same timestamped input log, when the log is replayed, then the same states result.
- Every play writes a JSONL session (header, steps, end) labelled by creator.

## Edge Cases & Rules

- Timer at any step is a function of recorded elapsed time (t_ms since session start).
- Rendering is a view of state, never a driver of it.

## UI / Feedback

- Game menus list levels and Test Levels with a start action.
- Debug readout shows the last registered input.

## Assets & Level Data Needed

- Sprites: reuse level-preview sprites from tools/static/level-sprites.
- Level JSON: existing levels/*.json format (rows + legend).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] game.html renders a chosen level.
- [ ] Same log replays to the same states.
- [ ] Every play writes a JSONL session.
- [ ] A Test Level can be launched from the game menu.

## Out of Scope

- Movement, timer-loss, keys, orbs and warp mechanics (later features).
- Procedural level generation.

## Open Questions

- Session file layout is fixed by the project-manager plan (header/steps/end/annotations).

## Testing

Needs a mechanics playground: reuse — the game menu must launch Test Levels; no dedicated room for this feature itself. Verification should record play sessions for replay.
